title: kv residency governor and fragmentation healing paths
author: Ayesha Kapoor
description: Motivation: persistent fragmentation and reactive full-spill behavior observed on multi-tenant workloads caused elevated P99 latency and repeated cold spills under transient load bursts. This PR introduces the 'Residency Governor'—a lightweight tenant-aware residency quota and healing controller that smooths demotion, schedules compact-on-read windows, and stages spillback to a deferred zero-copy spill pipeline to avoid synchronous eviction stalls. Changes include: a) quota-based per-tenant soft reservations with backpressure signals to the scheduler; b) probabilistic fragmentation scoring to trigger low-impact 'healing' compactions rather than full-page reclaims; c) compact-on-read heuristic that opportunistically compacts hot fragmented segments during KV reads to amortize work; d) graceful spill staging: small pages are batched into a spill queue and written asynchronously with backoff, reducing tail stalls; e) minor kernel-path annotations to favor eviction-friendly page shapes to reduce fragmentation over time. Checklist: - [x] design doc updated (docs/ops/kv-residency-governor.md); - [x] unit + integration tests added; - [x] benchmark harness: microbench and end-to-end spike tests; - [x] added feature flag for gradual rollout. Related: ENG-7192 design discussions and a postmortem reference at SUP-1114. This description summarizes the implementation, tests, and measured impact (see CI/perf).

release_notes: Introduce Residency Governor: tenant-aware soft reservations to reduce synchronous spills.
Enable compact-on-read to amortize compaction work and reduce long-tail evictions.
Staged asynchronous spill writer to lower eviction-induced latency spikes.
Default behavior behind feature flag kv_residency_governor=false; gradual rollout planned across Dedicated clusters.
